interpretation.reproduced: Five observations of the five supplied links are recorded: 2026-11-17 (prior sessions), 2026-11-20 by arena-23d7ed19, 2026-11-20 by arena-82d39deb, 2026-11-20 by arena-c2123b9c (S29, 5/5 matched) and 2026-11-20 by arena-9a3bb152 (1/5 matched — the other four tokens landed on the Amazon homepage; FLG-026). Four of five runs agree 5/5 with the recorded mapping; the observed_* fields rest on those runs, and the divergent run is published rather than dropped. FLG-008 stays closed: no run contradicted a previously recorded target, one run simply failed to reproduce it from that client.
interpretation.what_reproduction_does_not_prove: Every final URL in the first three observations carried lv=shuf (shuffle) and plpRedirect=mhFallback (listing-page fallback). That is a fallback route, not a canonical resolution of the submitted token. The targets were stable per token across the first three observations, so they are a usable observation — but they do not confirm that the person who supplied the links intended these five products, and the fourth observation shows the behavior can differ from one run to the next. Intended fields therefore stay blank.
interpretation.operational_consequence: Keep publishing without reader links until the Associates one-link test (FLG-002) confirms destination and tracking report. If the owner confirms the five products are the intended ones, nothing about the pages changes except the intended_* fields and confirmation_date. Third observation also re-read each listing's product-details table: one recorded row was wrong (the 8-quart Chefman's wattage — FLG-022, corrected) and four listing-internal contradictions were confirmed (FLG-005, FLG-010, FLG-018, FLG-020). Fifth recorded observation (FLG-026): destination must be re-checked from a normal browser and inside the enrolled Associates workflow test (FLG-002) before any short link is used at scale.
